question.text: A personal loan of Rs. 2,00,000 is taken at 14% p.a. for 3 years with monthly EMI. The total interest paid over the loan tenure is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: Monthly rate = 14%/12 = 0.011667. Using the PMT formula on Rs. 2,00,000 for 36 months gives EMI of about Rs. 6,835.53. Total paid = 6,835.53 x 36 = approximately Rs. 2,46,079. Total interest = 2,46,079 - 2,00,000 = about Rs. 46,079. Among the listed options, Rs. 46,368 is the closest value. The Trap: Rs. 84,000 is simple interest (2,00,000 x 14% x 3). Loan EMIs reduce the principal gradually, so interest accrues on a reducing balance and the total is less than simple interest on the full amount. Note: Small differences from Rs. 46,368 arise from rounding the EMI; the PMT-based total interest is about Rs. 46,079.
